description: A bearded warrior in a plumed helmet and dark armour rides a dark horse, raising a curved sword, with a round shield on his arm. Behind him is a crenellated fortress gate with a glowing arched entrance. Mounted riders with lances and pennant flags follow through a firelit dusk, and a domed mosque with minarets sits in silhouette under a stormy blue sky. The style is an oil painting with warm firelight, with no visible text beyond a small sparkle logo in the bottom-right corner, and no frame or border.
reason: Shows a mounted warrior riding out of a fortified gate, with no caravanserai, merchants, pack animals or trade goods, so the picture does not show Silk Road trade or a roadside inn. The red sandstone walls, domes and tall minarets look South Asian (Mughal or later) rather than the blue-tiled Timurid architecture of Samarkand around 1400, so the setting and era need a second look.
